notes.text: Coastal chemical site (in a designated industrial disaster-prevention district) producing high-purity polycrystalline silicon (semiconductor grade, about 2,800 t/yr across two plants), silicon tetrachloride (STC), trichlorosilane (TCS) and dichlorosilane (DCS).
Chlorination: metallurgical silicon powder (about 98% Si) reacts with HCl in a fluidised-bed furnace at about 300 °C to give mainly TCS plus H2 (some STC).
Distillation: multi-stage columns purify TCS, including chlorosilanes recovered from hydrogen recovery.
Deposition: vaporised TCS mixed with H2 deposits Si on heated thin silicon rods (surface about 1,000 °C).
Hydrogen recovery: reactor off-gas (unreacted TCS, H2, STC, HCl) is cooled so that chlorosilanes condense; H2 is purified and recycled.
Finishing: cutting, crushing, etching, washing, drying, inspection, packing.
System pressure about 0.1 MPa (gauge/absolute not stated).
By-product STC is sent to a neighbouring company, which returns HCl from its own production.

History: 3 years ago a burn injury during dismantling of an exchanger (corrective actions not followed up). 2 years ago an explosion in the drainage tank facility when NaOH contacted residue from dismantling and cleaning a gas-gas exchanger; attributed to fast hydrogen release from polymer plus alkali, and judged not possible without alkali.
Hazard levels of non-routine work are not classified; training does not cover polymer hazards.

Hydrogen recovery train (unit HR-6): demister (removes solids) → water-cooled exchangers HX-A / HX-B / HX-C → gas-gas exchanger GG-1 → low-temperature exchanger LT-1 → condensate tanks → hydrogen purification (HCl separated and recovered, H2 purified).
Heat-exchanger washing area: open area enclosed with flame-retardant resin sheeting, temporary floodlights, temporary high-pressure jet-water tank and pump; timber supports for exchangers.
Washing area is in the open within the plant, near the activated carbon unit and the No. 2 crude distillation pipe rack.
Next day: disconnected and moved to the temporary storage area.

HX-A, HX-B, HX-C water-cooled exchangers (three lines; normally two running, one standby). Each: vertical shell-and-tube, installed upright; process gas in at the upper channel cover, down through the tubes, out at the lower channel cover via an L-shaped outlet pipe; cooling water in at the lower shell, out at the upper shell. Heat-transfer area 101 m² (tube ID basis); 293 tubes, OD 34 mm, ID 28.2 mm, length 4,000 mm; outer dimensions 912 mm diameter × 5,996 mm long; weight 4,800 kg empty, 6,300 kg operating. Shell and channel covers SUS304; tubes and tubesheets SUS316L. Upper channel cover about 300 kg, bolted at a flange, carries the gas inlet valve. Operating temperature and pressure not stated.

Chlorosilane polymers (compounds with chains of two or more Si atoms, formed from SiCl2 produced in the deposition reactors) deposit on the tube inner walls of HX-A/B/C during operation, narrowing the flow path. Changeover to the standby exchanger is decided from outlet temperature and pressure drop, and a fixed service period has applied for the last 3 years.

notes.text: The work standard gives no quantitative end-point for the hydrolysis step. Work standards are approved by the section manager and may be changed within the section.

steps.text: Seven weeks ago: HX-B taken out of service; cooling water drained; process side purged with dry nitrogen.
Next day: disconnected and moved to the temporary storage area.
Over the following week, on three days: dry nitrogen blow at 20 Nm³/h and 0.018 MPa (gauge/absolute not stated) to remove residual chlorosilanes, HCl and H2.

Then 20 working days, about 09:00–17:00 each day: humidified nitrogen blow (about 0.8 vol% H2O) to hydrolyse the polymer surface so that less HCl and H2 is released at opening; no temperature control (ambient, winter conditions). Total water introduced about 11 kg.
The last three days: dry nitrogen blow to remove HCl and H2 formed by hydrolysis.
About 07:30: fill HX-B process side with dry nitrogen to a slight positive pressure; close valves.
About 09:00: move HX-B to the washing area with the gas inlet and outlet pointing upward; replace the channel-cover flange bolts beforehand (seized bolts delay opening).
Connect dry-nitrogen hoses to both channel covers; blow nitrogen at 20 Nm³/h and 0.018 MPa; draw exhaust from the underside of the lower cover to the NaOH scrubber.
With nitrogen blowing, remove the L-shaped outlet pipe; remove the lower channel cover with the crane truck; wash with normal- and high-pressure water; cover the opening with vinyl sheet.
Afternoon: remove the gas inlet valve from the upper channel cover; open the upper channel cover, hung from the crane truck; wash the tubes with high-pressure water.

notes.text: People: a production safety manager directing seven production staff; an equipment-department construction officer with three staff; a contractor site supervisor with six workers and one crane-truck operator. Other staff will attend around the exchanger to observe and for training.
